# Map — godkit

**Generated:** 2026-08-22T14:17:00.946Z · **Commit:** 4f151d80 · **Nodes:** 143

Zero-runtime-dependency Node.js harness that coordinates Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, and Gemini-compatible agents through committed .agent state. Host rule or SessionStart hook -> shared BOARD/map/log context -> CLI and skill workflows -> verified task handoff. Project maps and skill evidence are Markdown/JSON files backed by Git; there is no database or application authentication layer.

**Stack:** JavaScript, Markdown, TOML, YAML, JSON

## Architecture

### Shared protocol and state

Canonical collaboration rules and the templates copied into each project's .agent directory. Host runtime policy belongs in hooks or skills, not in these state shapes.

- `AGENTS.md` — Canonical always-on collaboration protocol for every host: inspect shared .agent state, claim file scopes before edits, and log verified outcomes at clock-out. The other host-specific rule files are generated from this one.
- `CLAUDE.md` — Generated Claude-facing copy of AGENTS.md. It carries the full shared-state and file-ownership protocol so Claude sessions receive it without relying on hooks alone; edit AGENTS.md and regenerate instead of changing this file.
- `.agents/rules/godkit.md` — Generated Antigravity-facing copy of the canonical AGENTS.md protocol. It is byte-for-byte rule content for a host with no hook enforcement, so changes belong in AGENTS.md and the sync generator.
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md` — Generated GitHub Copilot-facing copy of the canonical AGENTS.md collaboration rules. It exists as a host adapter and must be regenerated from AGENTS.md rather than edited independently.
- `templates/BOARD.md` — Canonical one-screen shared-state template for agent roster, exclusive file claims, active tasks, known bugs, binding decisions, and the three latest handoffs.
- `templates/THREAD.md` — Append-only inter-agent message template for timestamped, attributed, task-linked actionable communication, including recipients and blockers.
- `templates/task.md` — Per-task lifecycle template defining ownership, file scope, exit condition, phase, and structured Plan, Execute, Review, Test, and Handoff evidence sections.
- `templates/log.md` — Session-log template with agent, session, timing, scope, status, and skill frontmatter plus sections for work, verification, bugs, decisions, and remaining handoff context.
- `templates/MAP.md` — Initial placeholder project-map template that marks the map as not built and directs an agent to run the godkit-map workflow.
- `templates/rules/cursor-header.md` — Cursor-rule frontmatter template that marks generated Godkit rules as always active with an empty glob filter and a shared-protocol description.

### CLI and core runtime

The zero-dependency implementation for project discovery, map scanning/persistence/freshness, project-skill evidence, and lazy-mode state. Host registration details stay outside this layer.

- `bin/godkit.js` — Zero-dependency CLI entry point for scaffolding shared state, installing host adapters, scanning and saving maps, managing project skills, reporting evidence, diagnosing setup, and uninstalling packaged skills. Map saves deliberately write graph, Markdown projection, then metadata so an interrupted save cannot advertise itself as complete.
- `lib/paths.js` — Central location and git utility used by the CLI and hooks. It finds the nearest existing .agent first, otherwise routes linked worktrees to the main repository root, and exposes every shared-state path plus sortable log naming.
- `lib/scan.js` — Deterministic filesystem scanner that categorizes authored files, applies hard skips plus a documented subset of .agentignore/.gitignore, and regex-extracts resolvable relative imports. Unknown types and files over 400 KiB are intentionally absent from the map input.
- `lib/batch.js` — Greedy deterministic clusterer for semantic-analysis calls. It favors import-connected files, then same-directory neighbors, under a 60 KiB budget while guaranteeing every non-data file is placed once even when one file exceeds budget.
- `lib/graph.js` — Persistence and projection layer for project memory: guarded graph loading, portable path sanitization, node/edge normalization, saving, structural signatures, and generated MAP.md rendering. Node IDs are identity, duplicate nodes resolve last-wins, and dangling edges are dropped.
- `lib/freshness.js` — Separates cheap git-based staleness detection from rebuild-scope classification. Changes under .agent are excluded so writing the map cannot immediately stale itself.
- `lib/evolve.js` — Implements project-local skill discovery, safety scanning, ownership-aware host linking, log-derived trust/evidence, capture-candidate clustering, and SKILLS.md rendering. Its ownership guard is the safe replacement boundary: only exact links into .agent/skills or marked copies may be removed.
- `lib/lazy.js` — Centralizes lazy-mode configuration, runtime state, host-specific hook output, and instruction loading. Runtime mode is stored in one host-wide .godkit-lazy-active file, so concurrent sessions currently share and overwrite the same state.

### Hook enforcement

Fail-open lifecycle handlers that brief arriving sessions, track lazy policy, watch map freshness, and require handoff evidence. Installation and registry files adapt the same handlers to hook-capable hosts.

- `hooks/brief.js` — Fail-open SessionStart briefing hook that injects BOARD, map freshness, project-skill trust/safety, two recent logs, and the THREAD tail, capped at 8,000 characters. If no .agent directory exists it explains how to initialize one instead of crashing the session.
- `hooks/clockout.js` — Stop hook that blocks once when the git worktree has non-.agent changes but no session-matching handoff log. It deliberately does not block clean, committed, non-git, or already-blocked sessions.
- `hooks/map-watch.js` — Fail-open PostToolUse hook that only checks freshness after shell commands likely to land git history. It emits additional context for stale or unbuilt maps and stays silent for unrelated commands.
- `hooks/lazy-activate.js` — Fail-open SessionStart hook that resolves the configured godkit-lazy default, records the active session mode, and injects its instructions. An off default clears stale mode state and emits nothing.
- `hooks/lazy-mode-tracker.js` — UserPromptSubmit hook for live lazy-mode control. It parses slash-command switches, persists an explicit default, reports the current mode, and recognizes plain-language deactivation while otherwise staying silent.
- `hooks/lazy-subagent.js` — SubagentStart hook that propagates the active lazy ruleset into delegated workers. An optional case-insensitive agent-type regex narrows injection; invalid regex or unreadable payload fails open so the discipline is not silently lost.
- `hooks/install.js` — Standalone settings merger for installing or uninstalling Godkit hooks in Claude/Codex-style JSON settings. It preserves foreign groups, identifies its own groups by script path, refuses malformed JSON, and backs up an existing settings file; the hook list is duplicated here rather than read from godkit-hooks.json.
- `hooks/godkit-hooks.json` — Shared Claude/Codex plugin hook registry. It wires six scripts to SessionStart, Stop, PostToolUse, SubagentStart, and UserPromptSubmit with portable regex-compatible matchers and bounded timeouts.

### Skills and analysis prompts

Installable behavior guides plus the specialized prompts that turn scans into a knowledge graph. Executable safety and state mutation remain in JavaScript, not prompt text.

- `agents/file-analyzer.md` — Prompt and schema contract for turning one scan batch into graph nodes and observed edges. It requires every assigned file to be read, stable relative-path IDs, actionable summaries, no guessed relationships, and exactly one scratch JSON output.
- `agents/architect.md` — Prompt contract for the architecture synthesis pass after batch graphs are merged. It derives project metadata, 3-8 named layers, and a 5-9 step start-here tour without inventing framework or runtime claims.
- `skills/godkit/SKILL.md` — Primary tech-lead arrival and orchestration protocol: inspect shared state, synthesize work, cut file-boundary seams, route them by capability and cost, verify results, and clock out. Its non-negotiables are reading the board, claiming scope, verifying delegation, and logging work.
- `skills/godkit-plan/SKILL.md` — Defines multi-agent task decomposition into disjoint file-owned vertical seams, with explicit scope, exit conditions, verification, dependency order, capability-aware assignment, written task files, and join gates.
- `skills/godkit-execute/SKILL.md` — Five-stage execution protocol covering preflight, deny-only guards, bounded action, independent verification, and checkpointing. Its recovery rule permits retries only after measurable state advancement and stops repeated or unproven loops.
- `skills/godkit-test/SKILL.md` — Defines the smallest meaningful verification strategy, prioritizing existing commands and focused assertions while requiring real output, regression coverage of both the symptom and sibling callers, and explicit evidence rather than claims.
- `skills/godkit-handoff/SKILL.md` — Authoritative shared-state and lifecycle protocol for BOARD, THREAD, task files, session logs, project skills, and generated maps. It defines clock-in/out, ownership collision rules, monotonic bug/task IDs, memory placement, and the join gate that makes work resumable across tools.
- `skills/godkit-map/SKILL.md` — Defines the incremental project-mapping workflow: classify freshness, scan and batch files, analyze nodes and edges, merge safely, derive architecture and tour data, then save graph, MAP, and metadata in crash-safe order.
- `skills/godkit-evolve/SKILL.md` — Procedure for capturing repeated project work, deriving narrow skill variants, and repairing skills blamed by logs under .agent/skills. It defines frontmatter, safety boundaries, audit/fix/autonomous gates, and evidence-based trust without claiming that self-reported correlation proves quality.
- `skills/godkit-git/SKILL.md` — Git mechanics for multi-agent work: isolated worktrees enforce disjoint claims, verified commits are checkpoints, and generated map conflicts are resolved by taking one valid side then regenerating. Shared append-oriented state is committed with the code it describes.
- `skills/godkit-lazy/SKILL.md` — Defines the godkit-lazy skill: choose the minimum viable implementation through a YAGNI/reuse/stdlib/native/dependency ladder, preserve safety and correctness boundaries, and verify non-trivial logic with one focused check.

### Host adapters and commands

Package manifests, command adapters, compatibility documentation, and generated host entrypoints. They expose canonical skills and hooks without implementing core behavior themselves.

- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` — Claude Code plugin manifest. It publishes the godkit package identity and points Claude at the shared hook registry rather than duplicating hook definitions.
- `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — Claude plugin marketplace entry for the local godkit package, including owner metadata, description, category, and local source root.
- `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` — Codex plugin manifest exposing the package's shared skills, agents, and hook registry. Keeping these as paths makes Codex consume the same canonical assets as the other hosts.
- `gemini-extension.json` — Antigravity/Gemini extension manifest. It exposes the packaged skills and agents directories and selects AGENTS.md as the extension context file.
- `commands/godkit.toml` — Top-level arrival command adapter: load shared state, refresh a stale map, synthesize and split the task, then claim scope before handling forwarded arguments.
- `commands/godkit-help.toml` — Argument-free command adapter that asks godkit-help to display the shared-state layout, ladders, skills, and CLI reference card.
- `docs/agent-portability.md` — Portability design note for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Antigravity: canonical asset ownership, per-host adapters, hook asymmetry, install paths, and the extension checklist. It explicitly marks Codex project-local skill discovery as not yet live-verified and explains why skills are linked individually rather than by folder.
- `README.md` — Primary user guide for the shared .agent protocol, four-host installation, hooks, CLI, project maps, project-local skills, and lazy modes. It also documents the zero-dependency design and the expected init-to-map workflow.

### Verification and release guards

Node test suites, generated-rule/version checks, package cleanup, and CI workflows. These prove the shipped artifact and shared contracts; they are not runtime dependencies.

- `package.json` — npm package and CLI contract for godkit: CommonJS, Node 18+, zero runtime dependencies, and bin/godkit.js as the executable. Its check/test scripts enforce generated-rule and cross-manifest version consistency before release.
- `scripts/check-versions.js` — CI/release guard that requires package, Claude plugin, Codex plugin, and Gemini extension manifests to share one semver and, on tag builds, match the pushed tag.
- `scripts/sync-rules.js` — Generates every host's always-on rule file from AGENTS.md, adding Cursor frontmatter only where required. --check turns the same projection into a CI drift detector.
- `scripts/uninstall.js` — Standalone cleanup script for globally installed skills, settings hooks, and the lazy flag. It currently recursively deletes any matching skill-name destination without ownership proof, removes whole hook groups when one command substring matches, and looks for obsolete ~/.codex/settings.json.
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` — Cross-platform CI workflow covering Ubuntu and Windows on Node 18, 22, and 24. Every matrix leg checks generated rules and versions before running npm test.
- `.github/workflows/publish.yml` — Release workflow for version tags or manual dispatch. It checks generated rules and manifest versions, runs the full test suite on Node 22, then publishes to npm with provenance and OIDC.
- `tests/package.test.js` — Package-contract tests for the published-file allowlist, executable CLI, zero runtime dependencies, skill and agent metadata, slash commands, synchronized versions and generated rules, hook configuration, and repository-reference hygiene.
- `tests/save.test.js` — CLI integration tests for graph save behavior, including graph/MAP/meta output, partial retention versus full replacement, corruption and missing-input refusal, tmp cleanup, path privacy, and freshness status.
- `tests/hooks.test.js` — Behavior tests for brief, clockout, and map-watch hooks across setup and malformed input, shared-state injection, dirty-worktree blocking, stop-hook loop prevention, agent-only changes, and stale-map warnings.
- `tests/evolve.test.js` — End-to-end tests for project-local skill evolution, covering audit and autonomous linking, safe unlinking, authored-skill protection, trust evidence, blame, quarantine, revision resets, coverage, candidate capture, doctor output, and brief-hook reporting.

## Start here

1. **Enter through the CLI** — bin/godkit.js is the executable surface for init, install, map, evidence, doctor, and uninstall operations; start here to see every supported workflow.
2. **Resolve project and shared state** — lib/paths.js decides which worktree and .agent directory every CLI command or hook reads, so its boundary rules affect the whole package.
3. **Follow the map pipeline** — scan -> batch -> graph persists the portable project map, while freshness decides whether the next analysis is partial, architectural, or full.
4. **Understand project-owned learning** — lib/evolve.js turns .agent skills and session logs into guarded host projections, trust status, and capture candidates.
5. **See session enforcement** — The hook registry routes session events into brief, clockout, map-watch, and lazy handlers; lib/lazy.js currently owns their shared mode state.
6. **Trace each host adapter** — Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and Copilot consume the same skills and rules through small manifests, TOML commands, and generated rule copies.
7. **Prove what ships** — package.json and the Node tests enforce zero dependencies, complete artifacts, synchronized manifests, hook behavior, and safe map persistence before CI or publishing.

## Recall

Grep `.agent/graph.json`, never load it whole: search `"name"`, `"summary"` and `"tags"`
for the concept, collect the node ids, then grep those ids in `"edges"` for the one-hop
neighbourhood. That answers most questions without reading a single source file.
